items.q: Match the timeline in Alport syndrome with the feature — 1) 5 years  2) 10 years  3) 10–15 years  4) 25–30 years … A) Asymptomatic microhematuria  B) Proteinuria + hypertension  C) ESRD  D) Creatinine rises
items.exp: Timeline: 5 years asymptomatic microhaematuria; 10 years proteinuria + hypertension; 10–15 years rising creatinine; 25–30 years ESRD. (Book p783)

items.q: A 12-year-old boy with a strong family history of renal failure has a rising serum creatinine. On the clinical-features table, at which point in the timeline does this occur?
items.exp: The Alport timeline places 'creatinine ↑' at 10–15 years, after microhaematuria at 5 years and proteinuria with HTN at 10 years. (Book p783)

items.q: The earliest renal manifestation in Alport syndrome (5 years) is asymptomatic microhematuria.
opts: False — the earliest feature is nephrotic-range proteinuria
False — the earliest feature is ESRD
True, but it begins only after 10 years
items.exp: Timeline, 5 years: asymptomatic microhaematuria; proteinuria with hypertension appears only at 10 years. (Book p783)

items.q: The ENT manifestation of Alport syndrome at 15 years is sensorineural hearing loss that characteristically begins at:
opts: Low frequency (the commonest pattern), then progresses to high frequency
High frequency (the commonest pattern), then progresses to low frequency
Sudden total deafness in the first year of life
items.exp: ENT manifestation at 15 years: SNHL of low frequency (m/c) which subsequently becomes high frequency. (Book p783)

items.q: Fill up: The hearing loss of Alport syndrome is sensorineural, abbreviated ______.
items.exp: Alport syndrome produces SNHL (sensorineural hearing loss), initially low frequency, later high frequency. (Book p783)

items.q: A 20-year-old man with Alport syndrome is examined at the slit lamp. The pathognomonic ocular sign is:
opts: Anterior lenticonus with an oil droplet appearance
items.exp: Ocular manifestations at 20 years: anterior lenticonus (pathognomonic), with an oil droplet appearance on slit lamp. (Book p783)

items.q: Fill up: The pathognomonic ocular manifestation of Alport syndrome is anterior ______.
items.exp: Anterior lenticonus — marked pathognomonic in the table — with an oil droplet appearance on slit lamp at 20 years. (Book p783)

items.q: The ocular findings described in Alport syndrome are an oil droplet appearance on slit lamp and anterior lenticonus.
opts: False — the described finding is a cherry-red spot
False — the described finding is a Kayser–Fleischer ring
True, but only in the AD form
items.exp: Ocular manifestations at 20 years: anterior lenticonus (pathognomonic) and oil droplet appearance on slit lamp. (Book p783)

items.q: All but one of the following appear in the Alport clinical-features timeline. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: The 5-year entry is asymptomatic microhaematuria; proteinuria (with HTN) appears at 10 years, and ESRD at 25–30 years. (Book p783)

items.q: A patient with Alport syndrome presents at 27 years with uraemic symptoms — fitting the last row of the clinical-features table, which reads:
items.exp: The final timeline row of the Alport table is ESRD at 25–30 years. (Book p783)
